title: Accessibility Features 101 - Tools and Tips for Every Student
event: DCR x Writing Center Collaborative Workshop
blurb: Introducing students to free and open-source text to speech tools and built-in accessibility features on common software and platforms.

featured_slides.note: The session establishes a working definition centered on minimizing physical and mental effort, positioning these tools as universal design principles rather than niche accommodations. This perspective invites all learners to view interface adjustments as standard productivity strategies for managing fatigue.

Visual pattern recognition gaps reveal why automated text extraction frequently misinterprets complex layouts, necessitating human review. This reality emphasizes that digital conversion tools serve best as starting points rather than finished products for academic materials.

Concluding with a focus on cognitive preservation, the presentation warns against allowing format management to overshadow actual learning objectives. It advocates for pragmatic trade-offs that ensure assistive workflows remain sustainable habits rather than exhausting administrative tasks.
